To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the factors associated with high-frequency use of emergency departments (ED) and ambulatory care among substance-using adults are gender, race, homelessness, a history of substance abuse treatment, chronic medical conditions (seizures, hepatitis B and C), and HIV/AIDS.

high-frequency use of the ED (> or =3 visits) was associated with being female, being African American, being homeless, having a history of multiple substance abuse treatment episodes, and having > or =1 ambulatory care visits.

the factors that predict high-frequency ED use among substance users are being female, being African-American, being homeless, having a history of substance abuse treatment episodes, having multiple ambulatory care visits, and having certain chronic conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of factors that are predictive of high-frequency use of medical care among substance-using adults.
understanding the utilization of medical services in a population of substance users.
identifying high-frequency users and factors that may be associated with such use among medically ill substance using adults.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
substance-using patients with chronic conditions, such as seizure disorder, hepatitis B or C, and HIV/AIDS, who access ambulatory care are less likely to utilize ED services at a high frequency.
substance abuse and mental illness are not the primary drivers for frequent ED utilization among this population.
substance use is associated with a high frequency of medical care use, particularly ED use.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
high frequency of ED use is associated with being female, African-American, homeless, and having a history of >1 substance abuse treatment episodes.
high-frequency use of emergency departments (ED) by substance-using patients is associated with a history of substance abuse treatment and homelessness.
substance abuse treatment is a key to reducing high-frequency utilization of ED.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of ambulatory and emergency care is not necessarily an indication of poor quality of care or poor outcomes.
substance-using adults are more likely to utilize high-frequency EDs than ambulatory care.
substance abuse treatment and chronic disease management are important factors to consider in the care of substance-using patients.
